hub.speaker: The Hunter
hub.text: Hollow's not safe alone. Hasn't been for weeks. The witch? Her business is hers and I keep to mine. Wolves took two lambs this spring — that's the whole of my trade.

text_variants.text: Still headed that way? Say when. I'm not doing anything the fields need me for today.
Didn't figure we'd both still be standing after that. Hollow's not the only thing that gets ugly once the sun's down out here, and now you've seen it firsthand.

options.text: The deer stopped at the treeline. Why?

options._comment: REPORT ROWS all carry heard_thicket_keeps beside their route counter: hut_ward_scrap has no quest-start gate, so a mage PC could read the scrap on a wander and settle thicket_answered for a quest never offered, firing 'New quest'/'Quest complete' back to back. Stated on all three so a later ungated producer cannot leak either.
options.text: The line's a ward. An old one, gone sour.
Fences are moved. The herd's got its road.
Whatever was denning on the line isn't anymore.

options._comment: R2 TALK-route RE-ENTRY, APPENDED LAST so cursor-pinned canonicals keep their indices. The start row is hide_when heard_thicket_keeps, the counter it banks, so thicket_brief/thicket_sign (herd_rerouted, the whole TALK route, and the hut pointer) were reachable only inside the accept conversation; leaving early orphaned them permanently while the beat still read 'Read the sign with the hunter'. Tallyman shape: requires the quest, hides on the route's terminal counter.
options.text: Take me back to that line in the thicket.

agreed.speaker: The Hunter
agreed.text: Figured. Bring your own bandages — I've got enough of my own to worry about.

thicket_brief.speaker: The Hunter
thicket_brief.text: Corusdeer. Whole herd came down off the north road and stopped dead at the old line in the thicket. Wouldn't cross it, wouldn't spook, just turned and walked back the way they came. Deer don't hold a line unless something taught them to. I lost two lambs to something with thorns for teeth this spring, so you'll forgive me for not walking in there on my own.

thicket_sign.speaker: The Hunter
thicket_sign.text: Here. Hoof marks come up, stop, turn, and go back, all along one line you can't see from standing. Not one print past it in a mile of treeline. Whatever's holding them isn't teeth. Teeth leave a mess.

options.text: Then we move the fences, not the deer.

thicket_rerouted.speaker: The Hunter
thicket_rerouted.text: Warn the fields, shift two fences, and the herd keeps its road for the winter. That's the whole of it. Nobody thanks you for work they can't see afterward. The deer will, in their way.

thicket_topic.speaker: The Hunter
thicket_topic.text: Know that treeline better than the headman does. He'd rather not. There's a hut the far side of the hollow nobody's opened in years, and whatever's drawn on that line was drawn by whoever kept it. Start there if you're the reading sort.

thicket_reported_read.speaker: The Hunter
thicket_reported_read.text: A ward. Somebody scratched a line in the dirt a hundred years back and the deer still read it better than I do. That's the first thing anyone's told me about that thicket that wasn't a guess.

thicket_reported_rerouted.speaker: The Hunter
thicket_reported_rerouted.text: Fences before deer. My father would have said the same and then done the opposite. Herd's watering at the north bend now, where I can see them. I'll sleep better for it, which is more than the hollow's given me lately.

thicket_reported_cleared.speaker: The Hunter
thicket_reported_cleared.text: Denning right on the line, of course it was. Line's still there and the deer still won't cross it, so we've learned exactly one thing and killed the other. I'll take one thing.
